title: Code Understanding is a Bottleneck for Coding Agents
title_zh: CABRA: 用于严格评估智能体编码能力的蓝图

paragraphs.en: Repository benchmarks (e.g., SWE-bench) for coding agents often assume that lines of code edited can predict task difficulty, but such datasets’ poor control over code and task types makes it hard to know which abilities truly drive agent errors. We present Cabra : a Coding Ability Blueprint for Rigorous Agent evaluation. Cabra builds tasks from scratch as call graph transformations and scales difficulty via a task size parameter on four axes: function traversal, search, runtime resolution, and instruction following. We run eight LLMs and six coding agents on 6,840 Cabra tasks to show: 1) LLM accuracy falls as task size grows, but agents stay near-perfect by offloading work to tools (e.g., \inlinecode grep); 2) Larger Cabra tasks elicit more tool calls for reading and analysis, while a separate study on SWE-bench Verified shows these tool call counts predict agents’ accuracy better than lines of code edited—suggesting task difficulty for agents can lie in understanding code to edit, not just in making edits; 3) Extending Cabra to an intense understanding task where models analyze divergent logic across two classes backs this finding, as agent accuracy finally falls. More broadly, we argue for synthetic evaluations like Cabra to unmask LLM weaknesses trivialized by tools (e.g., needle-in-a-haystack) and abilities beyond just editing (e.g., understanding) that coding agents still find difficult---pairing SWE-bench-style tasks with controlled diagnosis. 1 1 1 We release our code at: https://github.com/microsoft/CABRA
paragraphs.zh: 用于评估编码智能体的仓库基准测试（例如 SWE-bench）通常假设被编辑的代码行数量可以预测任务难度，但这些数据集对代码和任务类型的控制能力较弱，使得难以判断哪些能力真正导致了智能体的错误。 我们提出了 Cabra：一项用于严格评估智能体的编码能力蓝图。 Cabra 从基础开始构建任务，将其设计为调用图的转换，并通过一个任务规模参数在四个维度上调整难度：函数遍历、搜索、运行时解析和指令遵循。 我们在 6,840 个 Cabra 任务上运行了八款 LLM 和六款编码智能体，研究结果表明：1）随着任务规模增大，LLM 的准确率下降，而智能体通过将工作外包给工具（例如 \inlinecode grep）仍能保持近乎完美的表现；2）规模更大的 Cabra 任务会引发更多用于阅读和分析的工具调用，而一项针对 SWE-bench Verified 的独立研究则表明，这些工具调用次数比被编辑的代码行数量更能预测智能体的准确率——这说明智能体面临的难度可能在于理解需要编辑的代码，而不仅仅是执行编辑操作；3）我们将 Cabra 扩展为一个高强度理解任务，要求模型分析两个类别中相互分歧的逻辑，这一扩展验证了上述发现，因为此时智能体的准确率终于开始下降。 更广泛地说，我们主张采用像 Cabra 这样的合成评估方法，以揭示 LLM 在工具辅助下被弱化的弱点（例如“针在干草堆中”问题），以及编码智能体仍然难以应对的、超越单纯编辑能力的技能（例如理解能力）——同时结合 SWE-bench 风格的任务与受控的诊断分析。1 1 1 我们的代码已发布在：https://github.com/microsoft/CABRA

paragraphs.en: Coding agents execute user queries by reasoning about, editing, and running code ( Chen et al., 2021 ) . They are often evaluated on benchmarks where researchers collect GitHub repositories, then augment them with problem statements and test cases as issue resolution tasks ( Jimenez et al., 2024 ) .
paragraphs.zh: 编码智能体通过推理、编辑和运行代码来执行用户查询（Chen 等人，2021）。 它们通常在基准测试中进行评估：研究人员收集 GitHub 仓库，然后将其与问题描述和测试用例结合，作为问题解决的任务（Jimenez 等人，2024）。

paragraphs.en: Progress in coding agents requires knowing when agents fail, but repository-augmented benchmarks impede this. Tasks jointly differ in their code and task types, supporting only correlational analyses ( Mehtiyev and Assunção, 2026 ) that can misidentify why agents fail. For example, Deng et al. (2026) attribute agents’ low accuracy in SWE-Bench Pro to agents editing more code, but our analysis shows that agents also have low accuracy when they read, analyze, and test their codebases more ( section 4.3 ).
paragraphs.zh: 智能体编码的进步需要明确智能体何时会失败，但通过代码库增强的基准测试却阻碍了这一目标。 这些任务在代码和任务类型上同时存在差异，因此仅能支持相关性分析（Mehtiyev 和 Assunção, 2026），而这类分析可能错误地识别智能体失败的原因。例如，Deng 等人 （2026）将智能体在 SWE-Bench Pro 中准确率较低归因于其编辑了更多代码，但我们的分析表明，当智能体对代码库进行更多读取、分析和测试时，其准确率同样较低（第 4.3 节）。

paragraphs.en: To escape such confounders, researchers have long relied on synthetic tasks that isolate model abilities, enabling evaluations of how model performance on these abilities scales based on task size ( Merrill et al., 2020 ) . For example, Needle in a Haystack ( Kamradt, 2023 ) offers a controlled evaluation for long-context reasoning over adjustable corpus sizes. While prior work has extended this methodology to reasoning LLMs ( Motwani et al., 2026 ) and RL environments ( Stojanovski et al., 2025 ) , it has not yet been studied in coding agents with vastly different behavior, thanks to their ability to call tools.
paragraphs.zh: 为了规避这类干扰因素，研究人员长期以来一直依赖合成任务来隔离模型的能力，从而能够评估模型在这些能力上的表现如何随任务规模而变化（Merrill 等，2020）。 例如，“干草堆中的针”任务（Kamradt，2023）为可调节语料库规模的长上下文推理提供了受控的评估方法。 尽管先前的研究已将这种方法扩展到推理型大型语言模型（Motwani 等，2026）和强化学习环境（Stojanovski 等，2025），但由于编码智能体能够调用工具，其行为差异极大，因此该方法尚未在编码智能体中得到研究。

paragraphs.en: We present Cabra : a C oding A bility B lueprint for R igorous A gent evaluation, a framework for generating programming tasks from scratch. Unlike repository-based benchmarks that derive tasks from codebases, Cabra splits task design into two controllable steps: defining task types and defining how those tasks scale in size. We instantiate these two steps by generating programs from directed acyclic call graphs and transforming them into five task types (Figure 1 left, section 2.1 ), then scaling those tasks across four axes synthesized from prior work: function traversal, function search, runtime resolution, and instruction following (Figure 1 right, section 2.2 ).
paragraphs.zh: 我们提出 Cabra：一个用于严格智能体评估的编码能力蓝图，它是一个从头生成编程任务的框架。 与从代码库中衍生任务的仓库基准不同，Cabra 将任务设计分为两个可控步骤：定义任务类型，以及定义这些任务在规模上的扩展方式。 我们通过从有向无环调用图中生成程序并将其转化为五种任务类型（图 1 左侧，第 2.1 节）来实现这两个步骤，然后沿着从先前研究中综合而来的四个维度扩展这些任务：函数遍历、函数搜索、运行时解析和指令遵循（图 1 右侧，第 2.2 节）。

sents.en: We present Cabra : a C oding A bility B lueprint for R igorous A gent evaluation, a framework for generating programming tasks from scratch.

paragraphs.en: We generate 6,840 Cabra task instances of increasing sizes ( section 3 ), while controlling for program and task type. By varying one scaling axis at a time across many codebases and tasks, we can robustly surface axes that are hardest for models. We run eight LLMs and six coding agents in Copilot’s public harness ( section 3.2 ) on these tasks to discover how our scaling axes impact task accuracy for LLMs without tools versus agents with them ( section 3.1 ), and reveal opportunities for improving agents.
paragraphs.zh: 我们在控制程序和任务类型的同时，生成了 6,840 个规模递增的 Cabra 任务实例（第 3 节）。 通过在多个代码库和任务中逐次变化一个扩展维度，我们可以可靠地识别出模型最难处理的维度。 我们使用 Copilot 的公开测试框架（第 3.2 节）在这些任务上运行了八款 LLM 和六个编码智能体，以探究我们的扩展维度如何影响无工具的 LLM 与具备工具的智能体在任务准确性上的表现（第 3.1 节），并揭示改进智能体的机会。

paragraphs.en: While LLM accuracy falls on larger Cabra tasks, agents can sustain near-perfect scores by offloading work to tools, like \inlinecode grep to search long code ( section 4.1 ). To dig deeper, we label agents’ tool calls: to read, analyze, search, edit, or test code ( section 4.2 ). As task size grows, agents do not always edit more, contrary to prior explanations for low accuracy ( Deng et al., 2026 ) . Instead, they often spend more tokens on tools to read and analyze code— understanding code to edit. We further verify that this behavior, discovered using Cabra ’s synthetic tasks, generalizes to more realistic code editing tasks: analyses on SWE-bench Verified traces reveal that the number of tool calls an agent spends to understand code predicts task difficulty better than line edit count ( section 4.3 ).
paragraphs.zh: 尽管 LLM 在更大规模的 Cabra 任务中的准确性会下降，但智能体通过将工作外包给工具（例如使用 \inlinecode grep 搜索长代码，见第 4.1 节）仍能保持近乎完美的得分。 为了更深入地分析，我们对智能体的工具调用进行了分类：读取、分析、搜索、编辑或测试代码（见第 4.2 节）。 随着任务规模的增长，与以往对低准确性的解释相反，智能体并不总是进行更多编辑操作（Deng et al., 2026）。 相反，它们通常会消耗更多令牌来使用工具读取和分析代码——即通过理解代码来进行编辑。 我们进一步验证了这种行为的普适性：这种通过 Cabra 的合成任务发现的行为也适用于更真实的代码编辑任务；对 SWE-bench Verified 轨迹的分析表明，智能体为理解代码所花费的工具调用次数比行编辑次数更能预测任务的难度（见第 4.3 节）。

paragraphs.en: Based on our analyses, we hypothesize that understanding-intensive tasks with relatively few edits can challenge agents. To causally test this hypothesis, we extend Cabra to a new task that targets and controls the amount of code that agents must understand: given two classes, extract all shared logic and preserve any differences ( section 5.1 ). When task size grows, agent accuracy falls, tokens spent on understanding tools balloon, and edits stay small—supporting code understanding as a weakness ( section 5.2 ). Follow-up analyses suggest agents fail to reason over logical decomposition, over-rely on surface-level naming, and struggle to excise one-line differences.
paragraphs.zh: 基于我们的分析，我们推测，需要深度理解但修改次数相对较少的任务可能会给智能体带来挑战。 为了对这一假设进行因果性检验，我们将 Cabra 扩展到一个新任务中，该任务专门针对并控制智能体必须理解的代码量：给定两个类，提取所有共享逻辑并保留任何差异（第 5.1 节）。 随着任务规模增大，智能体的准确率下降，用于理解工具的令牌数量激增，而修改次数却保持较少——这支持了代码理解是其弱点的观点（第 5.2 节）。 后续分析表明，智能体无法对逻辑分解进行推理，过度依赖表层命名，并且难以移除单行差异。

sents.en: Follow-up analyses suggest agents fail to reason over logical decomposition, over-rely on surface-level naming, and struggle to excise one-line differences.
sents.zh: 后续分析表明，智能体无法对逻辑分解进行推理，过度依赖表层命名，并且难以移除单行差异。

paragraphs.en: To control our baseline code editing tasks, we use directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) to represent programs, and then transform them to define code edits. Each DAG 𝒞 \mathcal{C} = ⟨ V , E ⟩ =\langle V,E\rangle is a function call graph, where v i ∈ V v_{i}\in V is a function and edge ( v i , v j ) ∈ E (v_{i},v_{j})\in E means v i v_{i} calls v j v_{j} . Each function computes a random mathematical function of its input. For v i v_{i} with many output vertices, v i v_{i} chains the function outputs with random operations. Appendix A.1 describes the sampling process. Figure 1 has example DAGs/programs with floats; we also design string and array versions so our analyses generalize beyond a single code type (Appendix A.2 has examples). We finally add a \inlinecode __main__ block calling the root vertex in 𝒞 \mathcal{C} . This synthetic code generation approach trades downstream realism for simplicity and tight control over tested coding abilities.

paragraphs.en: Runtime Resolution: Coding tasks may force models to trace increasingly long computations to resolve runtime values ( Gu et al., 2024 , e.g., CRUXEval) . To test this, we wrap an \inlinecode if check(): around identical code blocks and have models only edit blocks that run. We scale the size of resolving \inlinecode check() via a Collatz-based function ( Lagarias, 1985 ) whose \inlinecode for loop runs for n n steps (Code Block ), requiring n n steps of reasoning to resolve.
paragraphs.zh: 运行时解析：编码任务可能迫使模型追踪越来越长的计算过程，以解析运行时的值（Gu et al., 2024，例如 CRUXEval）。 为了验证这一点，我们在相同的代码块周围包裹一个 \inlinecode if check(): 判断，并让模型仅编辑实际运行的代码块。 我们通过一个基于 Collatz 的函数（Lagarias, 1985）来调整解析 \inlinecode check() 的规模，其 \inlinecode for 循环会运行 n n 步（代码块），因此需要 n n 步的推理才能完成解析。

paragraphs.en: We find that large Cabra tasks challenge LLMs but not agents due to tool use ( section 4.1 ). Agent traces show they spend many tokens on tools to understand code in larger tasks—not just edit it ( section 4.2 )—with similar trends in SWE-Bench ( section 4.3 ). We thus argue that scaling understanding effort is promising for making hard agentic coding tasks, which we test in section 5 .
paragraphs.zh: 我们发现，大型 Cabra 任务对 LLM 构成了挑战，但对智能体而言并非如此，这得益于工具的使用（第 4.1 节）。 智能体的追踪记录显示，在更复杂的任务中，它们会消耗大量 token 使用工具来理解代码，而不仅仅是编辑代码（第 4.2 节）；SWE-Bench 中也观察到了类似趋势（第 4.3 节）。 因此，我们认为扩大理解方面的投入有望让困难的智能体编程任务变得可行，我们将在第 5 节对此进行测试。

paragraphs.en: LLM-Hard ⇏ \nRightarrow Agent-Hard. LLM accuracy drops with n n , but agent accuracy is mostly constant and often near perfect. paragraphs.en: While prior work uses edits to predict coding task difficulty ( Deng et al., 2026 ; Raghavendra et al., 2026 ) , only instruction following elicits more Edit tokens with n n (Figure 3 ). Instead, Read and Analyze tokens grow for all axes but runtime. We treat these two as code understanding actions: acquiring knowledge of a program’s construction and reasoning about its behavior to guide later edits ( Littman et al., 1987 ; Maalej et al., 2014 ) . Their position in agent traces backs our interpretation: 48% of Read and 40% of Analyze calls occur in the first quarter, and 69% and 56%, respectively, precede the first Edit —the most of all tools. Search may support understanding, but work treats pattern-matching lookups ( \inlinecode grep) as distinct actions preceding understanding ( Wilde et al., 2001 ; Bennett et al., 2002 ) . Consistent with this idea, only 12% of Search tools are followed by Edit , but 19% are followed by Read .
paragraphs.zh: 尽管先前的研究利用编辑操作来预测编码任务的难度（Deng et al., 2026；Raghavendra et al., 2026），但只有指令遵循会引发更多 Edit 标记（图3）。 相反，Read 和 Analyze 标记在所有轴上均有所增长，唯独运行时除外。 我们将这两种操作视为代码理解行为：获取程序结构的知识，并推理其行为以指导后续编辑（Littman et al., 1987；Maalej et al., 2014）。 它们在智能体轨迹中的位置支持了我们的解释：48% 的 Read 调用和 40% 的 Analyze 调用发生在初始阶段，而 69% 和 56% 的调用分别出现在首次 Edit 之前——在所有工具中比例最高。 Search 可能有助于理解，但相关研究将模式匹配查询（\inlinecode grep）视为理解之前的独立操作（Wilde et al., 2001；Bennett et al., 2002）。 与此观点一致，仅有 12% 的 Search 工具后接 Edit，而 19% 的后接 Read。

paragraphs.en: Edits are not the scapegoat for human-rated difficulty. SWE-bench tasks come with difficulty levels based on the time developers estimate humans would need to finish them (L1 ≤ \leq 15 min; L2 = 15 min – 1 hr; L3 = 1–4 hours; L4 ≥ \geq 4 hours). Most metrics rise with level (Figure 4 , left): longer tasks elicit not just more edits, but also reading, analysis, and testing. Since metrics grow jointly, SWE-bench alone cannot discern when errors stem from edit volume or understanding how to edit—motivating controlled evaluations such as Cabra .
paragraphs.zh: 编辑操作并非人类评定难度时的替罪羊。 SWE-bench 任务的难度等级基于开发者估计的人类完成任务所需的时间（L1 ≤ \leq 15 分钟；L2 = 15 分钟 – 1 小时；L3 = 1–4 小时；L4 ≥ \geq 4 小时）。 大多数指标随难度等级升高而增加（图 4，左侧）：任务越复杂，不仅需要更多编辑操作，还需要更多的阅读、分析和测试。 由于各项指标会同步增长，仅凭 SWE-bench 无法区分错误究竟源于编辑次数过多，还是源于对如何编辑的理解不足——这促使了像 Cabra 这样的受控评估方法的出现。

Models start with classes 𝒞 A \mathcal{C}_{A} , 𝒞 B \mathcal{C}_{B} with ℓ \ell lines each that differ in behavior at d d lines: models must move the ℓ − d \ell-d equivalent lines into a parent class 𝒞 parent \mathcal{C}_{\text{parent}} and keep the d d differences in child classes (Figure 5 , left). As ℓ \ell grows, edits scale modestly (e.g., O ⁡ ( ℓ ) O(\ell) lines per class), but combinations of lines that can be understood to locate differences skyrockets (e.g., Ω ⁡ ( ℓ 2 ) \Omega(\ell^{2}) lines worst case). We later validate this intuition empirically: agents’ tool calls for Analyze rise sharply with ℓ \ell ( section 5.2 ).

paragraphs.en: 2) Aligning Logic. We hypothesize that our understanding task is hard as it requires aligning syntactically distinct but semantically equivalent code ( Churchill et al., 2019 ) . Thus, we test the equivalence transform types agents must align as complexity axes for understanding. We ablate transforms at ℓ = 50 \ell=50 : adding each to a no-transform baseline (Figure 6 , left) and removing each from an all-transform baseline (Figure 6 , middle). Multi-line edits and distributive multiplication cause large drops when added—for Gemini specifically (Appendix A.10 )—failing on multi-hop alignment ( Zhang et al., 2025a ) . Removing variable renaming boosts accuracy most, so agents may rely on shallow naming to understand code ( Lam et al., 2025 ) .
paragraphs.zh: 2) 逻辑对齐。 我们假设，我们的理解任务之所以困难，是因为它需要对语法上不同但语义上等价的代码进行对齐（Churchill 等，2019）。 因此，我们将智能体必须对齐的等价转换类型作为理解复杂性的维度进行测试。 我们在 ℓ = 50 \ell=50 处对转换进行了消融分析：将每种转换添加到无转换的基线模型中（图6，左），并从全转换的基线模型中移除每种转换（图6，中）。 当添加多行编辑和分配乘法时，准确率会大幅下降——尤其是在 Gemini 上（附录 A.10）——导致多跳对齐失败（Zhang 等，2025a）。 移除变量重命名对准确率的提升最大，因此智能体在理解代码时可能依赖浅层的命名方式（Lam 等，2025）。

paragraphs.en: 3) Locating Differences. When agents edit, they generally follow the two-step process of: (i) locating lines that differ; and (ii) executing the refactor. To disentangle where errors occur, we study both metrics in section 5.1 . Agents preserve code behavior in over 90% of cases, so most failures stem from (i) versus (ii); agents keep too many lines in the child class, failing to find one line differences. We further probe this weakness by varying the number of differing lines d ∈ { 1 , 3 , 5 } d\in\{1,3,5\} while holding lines of code ℓ \ell fixed. Accuracy erodes as d d grows (Figure 6 , right), validating agents struggle increasingly as they need to identify more behavioral differences.

paragraphs.en: Evaluating Code Models. Code generation is a long-studied task ( Hindle et al., 2012 ) . Early evaluations used NL-to-code translation tasks ( Oda et al., 2015 ; Yin et al., 2018 ) , then scaled difficulty with algorithm tasks based on contests like LeetCode ( Chen et al., 2021 ; Li et al., 2022 ; Jain et al., 2025 ) . The boom of agents that compose LLMs and tools ( Yao et al., 2023 ) motivated harder tasks like issue resolution ( Jimenez et al., 2024 ; Zan et al., 2025 ) and full app generation from specifications ( Si et al., 2025 ; Zhao et al., 2025 ) . paragraphs.en: Agent Failures. Knowing model failures drives progress. For coding agents, work often studies properties of failed traces on repository benchmarks ( Cemri et al., 2025 ) like execution strategy, tool call type, and length—relating them to agent accuracy to guide methods ( Majgaonkar et al., 2025 ; Liu et al., 2025b ; Mehtiyev and Assunção, 2026 ) . However, analyses are correlational—tasks also vary in codebase and task—making it hard to attribute failures, and correlations are often poor ( section 4.3 ). We argue Cabra -style tasks that control such confounders are better for this goal, which we use to surface agent weaknesses in code understanding.
paragraphs.zh: 智能体失败。 了解模型失败能够推动进步。 对于编码智能体，相关研究通常会分析仓库基准测试中失败轨迹的特性（Cemri 等，2025），例如执行策略、工具调用类型和长度，并将其与智能体的准确性联系起来，以指导方法改进（Majgaonkar 等，2025；Liu 等，2025b；Mehtiyev 和 Assunção，2026）。 然而，这些分析仅具有相关性——任务在代码库和具体任务上也存在差异，这使得归因失败变得困难，且相关性通常较弱（第 4.3 节）。 我们认为，采用 Cabra 风格的任务来控制此类混淆因素更有助于实现这一目标，因此我们使用这类任务来揭示智能体在代码理解方面的弱点。

paragraphs.en: Synthetic Tasks. Compared to repository benchmarks, synthetic tasks can better probe model errors ( Merrill et al., 2020 ) . Tasks like bAbI ( Weston et al., 2016 ; Tamari et al., 2022 ) and Needle in a Haystack ( Hsieh et al., 2024 ; Kim et al., 2025 ) test limits of a model ability (e.g., long-context) by defining tasks (e.g., locate a passkey) and scaling their size (e.g., corpus size); we use this two-stage approach for Cabra . Recent work extends this to reasoning LLMs: LongCoT for long-horizon execution ( Motwani et al., 2026 ) and RELIC for context-free grammar recognition ( Petty et al., 2026 ) . In code specifically, related work includes CruxEval for code tracing ( Gu et al., 2024 ) and Bug in the Code Stack for codebase search ( Lee et al., 2024 ) , which form our initial Cabra tasks. There are also synthetic RL environments to train coding agents ( Yang et al., 2025b ; Zhu et al., 2025 ) , but their use of existing repositories or LLM-generated data impede full control over tasks, unlike Cabra .
paragraphs.zh: 合成任务。 与代码库基准测试相比，合成任务能更有效地探测模型错误（Merrill 等，2020）。 像 bAbI（Weston 等，2016；Tamari 等，2022）和“干草堆中的针”（Hsieh 等，2024；Kim 等，2025）这样的任务，通过定义具体任务（例如，定位通行证）并调整其规模（例如，语料库大小），来测试模型能力的极限（例如，长上下文能力）；我们在 Cabra 中采用了这种两阶段方法。 近期的研究将这种方法扩展到了推理型大型语言模型：LongCoT 用于长时程执行（Motwani 等，2026），而 RELIC 则用于上下文无关文法识别（Petty 等，2026）。 在代码领域，相关研究包括用于代码追踪的 CruxEval（Gu 等，2024）和用于代码库搜索的“代码堆栈中的错误”（Lee 等，2024），这些构成了我们最初的 Cabra 任务。 此外，也存在用于训练编码智能体的合成强化学习环境（Yang 等，2025b；Zhu 等，2025），但这类环境使用现有代码库或由大型语言模型生成的数据，导致无法像 Cabra 那样对任务进行完全控制。

paragraphs.en: Different from all of these works, we explore task complexity in coding agents. Our main contribution is exposing that many “LLM-hard” tasks are trivial with tool use—task complexity must evolve for agents—then surfacing and probing code understanding as a model weakness.
paragraphs.zh: 与所有这些研究不同，我们探讨了编码智能体中的任务复杂性。 我们的主要贡献在于揭示了许多“LLM难题”在借助工具使用时其实非常简单——智能体的任务复杂性必须随之演变——进而暴露并深入探究代码理解能力作为模型弱点的表现。

paragraphs.en: Using Cabra , we show the number of edits alone is a poor proxy for coding agent task difficulty and instead surface code understanding as a key factor. Across our initial task axes, editing effort scales insufficiently with task size. In contrast, we reveal that code understanding more often scales with task size across diverse axes and more reliably predicts SWE-bench Verified errors. We establish this link concretely with our code merging task and surface facets like multi-line decomposition and readability where agents still struggle, motivating threads for future work.
paragraphs.zh: 通过 Cabra，我们发现仅凭编辑次数难以准确反映编码智能体任务的难度，而代码理解能力才是关键因素。 在我们初步设定的任务维度中，编辑工作量与任务规模的增长并不充分匹配。 相比之下，我们揭示出：在多种不同任务维度中，代码理解能力更常随任务规模同步增长，并且能更可靠地预测 SWE-bench Verified 错误。 我们通过代码合并任务具体确立了这一关联，并揭示了多行分解和可读性等智能体仍面临挑战的方面，从而为未来研究指明了方向。

paragraphs.en: Controlled Evaluation. Cabra -style tasks can both attribute agent error and form axes to probe them. We use tools for diagnosis, but future work can study problem-solving methods ( Gao et al., 2024 ) and error recovery ( Huang et al., 2024 ) . The next step is imbuing such weaknesses into SWE-bench-style tasks as more realistic evaluations ( Saxon et al., 2024 ) .
paragraphs.zh: 受控评估。 Cabra 风格的任务既能归因于智能体的错误，也能构建用于探测这些错误的维度。 我们使用工具进行诊断，但未来的研究可以探索问题解决方法（Gao 等人，2024）和错误恢复机制（Huang 等人，2024）。 下一步是将此类弱点融入 SWE-bench 风格的任务中，以实现更真实的评估（Saxon 等人，2024）。

paragraphs.en: Agent-Understandable Code. Agents struggle to compare programs with renamed variables ( section 5.2 ), showing some code types are harder to understand. Future work could test if repository indexes ( Luo et al., 2026 ) , memory ( Zhang et al., 2025b ) , and readability practices ( Buse and Weimer, 2009 ) help agents. As understanding can encompass up to 70% of SWE work ( Minelli et al., 2015 ) , 19% of real coding requests ( Baumann et al., 2026 ) , and already demands effort in Cabra and SWE-Bench, progress here is key for maintainability ( Le et al., 2026 ) and limiting context rot ( Laban et al., 2026a ) .

paragraphs.en: A Theory of Agents. Work on transformers’ limits ( Bhattamishra et al., 2020 ) often uses synthetic tasks like Cabra to empirically test theories, but tasks that were once hard for LLMs can now be trivial with tools ( section 4.1 ). Discerning “agent-hard” or “-easy” tasks will require formalizing the work used to call tools and work tools can execute ( Meyerson and Qiu, 2025 ) .
paragraphs.zh: 智能体理论。 关于 Transformer 模型局限性的研究（Bhattamishra 等人，2020）通常使用 Cabra 等合成任务来对理论进行经验验证，但曾经对大型语言模型具有挑战性的任务，如今借助工具却变得轻而易举（第 4.1 节）。 要区分“智能体困难”或“智能体简单”的任务，就需要将调用工具的工作以及工具能够执行的工作形式化（Meyerson 和 Qiu，2025）。

paragraphs.en: In this work, we used generative AI tools primarily for code implementation and data visualization (e.g., plots). We have not used generative AI for writing from scratch, figure generation, or designing the high-level framing and structure of this paper. We also minimally used generative AI tools for revising writing, brainstorming, reviewing our paper, and literature search. For coding, we have reviewed all AI-assisted work through a combination of manually defined test cases, and visualization tools to verify that our evaluations generate data, elicit model responses, and score responses correctly. Before releasing our code, one author reviewed all generative AI outputs to detect any errors. We take full responsibility for the final content of this work, including any errors from generative AI.

paragraphs.en: Our paper shows that coding agents can struggle to understand code. Given the importance of understanding in real developer workflows ( Minelli et al., 2015 ; Baumann et al., 2026 ) —coupled with evidence that programmers struggle to understand their code when working with agents ( Shen and Tamkin, 2026 ; Balepur et al., 2026a ) —there are risks for failing to address this problem. We hope that our paper brings more attention to evaluating understanding in coding agents.

paragraphs.en: Add a number: \inlinecode new_var = var + rand.

paragraphs.en: All models use the Completions API, except Codex (Responses API). paragraphs.en: When reviewing our agent traces, we found cases where our agents attempted to get information from other parallel runs (recalling the OpenAI security incident reported with Hugging Face ( OpenAI, 2026b ) ). In particular, we found that some agents used the Copilot CLI session store database to search for similar sessions (although this was very rare; only 72 / ∼ \sim 43k traces). Others explicitly searched the local filesystem for other agents’ solution.py . Attempts to read these files were permission-denied; however, all agents shared access to /tmp , which some used for intermediate tasks. paragraphs.en: Our evaluations with Cabra in section 4 reveal two task types where scaling complexity changes behavior in agent tool calls: 1) Understand tool calls increase while Edit tool calls remain stable (i.e., function search and function traversal); and 2) Both Understand and Edit tool calls increase (i.e., instruction following). paragraphs.zh: 我们在第 4 节中与 Cabra 进行的评估揭示了两种任务类型，在这些任务中，复杂度的提升会改变智能体工具调用的行为：1）“理解”工具调用增加，而“编辑”工具调用保持稳定（即函数搜索和函数遍历）；以及 2）“理解”和“编辑”工具调用均增加（即指令遵循）。 为了确认“理解”和“编辑”是相互独立的构建要素，我们现在设计了一项任务，该任务会随着复杂度的提升而增加对“编辑”的要求，同时“理解”的要求不会发生显著变化。
